stages.headline: The numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, ... used for counting objects are called natural numbers.
stages.headlineEnglish: The numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, ... used for counting objects are called natural numbers.

stages.headline: Natural numbers form the natural sequence. The smallest is 1; there is no largest.
stages.headlineEnglish: Natural numbers form the natural sequence. The smallest is 1; there is no largest.

stages.headline: Each natural number is followed by the number 1 greater. Every natural number except 1 has a predecessor.
stages.headlineEnglish: Each natural number is followed by the number 1 greater. Every natural number except 1 has a predecessor.

stages.headline: Three consecutive natural numbers add up to 36. Find the largest.
stages.headlineEnglish: Three consecutive natural numbers add up to 36. Find the largest.
stages.problemText: Three consecutive natural numbers add up to 36. Find the largest.
stages.solutionSteps: 1. The middle number is 36 : 3 = 12. 2. The numbers are 11, 12, 13. 3. The largest is 13.
stages.solutionStepsEnglish: 1. The middle number is 36 : 3 = 12. 2. The numbers are 11, 12, 13. 3. The largest is 13.
